sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72].
Revenue then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 to $44.0 billion [F6][D231] and 16.5% in FY2023 to a peak of $61.3 billion [F8][D322], before falling 15.6% in FY2024 [F9][D367] and 11.7% in FY2025 [F10][D412].
Operating margin followed the same shape, from 9.7% in FY2016 [F22] to a 21.2% high in FY2023 [F29] and 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], the last year the table reports it.
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], and it fell 17.6% in FY2025, subtracting 7.0pp from revenue growth [D658][D659].
The filing attributes the decline to sales volumes down 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% volume increase in Brazil [P10].

Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue [D889], fell 11.8% in FY2025 and subtracted 3.0pp [D890][D891], while Small Agriculture & Turf, 22.8% of revenue [D905], fell 7.0% and subtracted 1.5pp [D906][D907].
Small Agriculture & Turf profit fell on lower sales volumes and higher tariffs, partly offset by price realization [P8].

Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 16.9% CAGR to FY2024 against 6.2% for revenue to FY2025 [F159][F157], but the incremental operating margin turned negative in FY2024 at 41.1% [D388].
The FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% [F30] sat 5.4pp above the window median of 12.1% [D1335] and 3.7pp below the FY2023 high of 21.2% [F29][D1334].
The FY2024 margin fell 3.7pp [D378], with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D391][D390], as revenue growth trailed operating-cost growth by 3.7pp [D389].
Net margin fell 2.7pp in FY2025 to 11.0% [F50][D422], while the effective tax rate eased to 20.1% [D400] and interest expense of $3.2 billion [X82] weighed on the $6.3 billion pretax line [X92].
The FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50] was below the industrials peer median of 12.7% [D1352], at the 29th percentile of seven peers [D1351].
Operating cash flow was $7.5 billion in FY2025 [F80], free cash flow $6.1 billion [F100], and free cash flow was 1.21x net income [D402] against a window median of 0.91x [D1347].
The filing credits operating inflows to net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Capex was $1.4 billion, or 3.0% of revenue [F90][D397], and 0.61x D&A [D403], so free cash flow margin held at 13.4% [D398] against a 11.6% median [D1341].
Free cash flow margin ranked at the 57th percentile of seven peers against a 13.2% median [D1353][D1354], and free cash flow conversion at the 100th percentile against 0.95x [D1359][D1360].
Net debt was $5.5 billion at FY2025 [D407], down from $35.8 billion in FY2021 [D226], as total debt fell to $13.8 billion [D406] against $8.3 billion of cash [F140].
Net debt was 12.1% of revenue [D408], better than the industrials peer median net debt of 38.8% of revenue and at the 100th percentile of seven peers [D1358][D1357].
Buybacks and dividends of $2.9 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], and the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427] from 277.1 million to 271.7 million [X118][X119].
Return on average equity was 20.6% [D411], below the 28.3% peer median and at the 17th percentile of six peers [D1362][D1361].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [F9][F10], the first back-to-back decline in the window, and the 3-year revenue CAGR is -4.6% [D1348].
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [D657][D658], and the filing cites U.S. and Canada volumes down 30% [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% in FY2025 [D889][D890], a second consecutive decline after FY2024's 11.9% drop [D887].
The FY2017 SG&A figure of $3,066.6 million [X34] was later reported at a higher value, a data-quality note that does not change the conclusions here.
Watch whether FY2026 revenue holds above the FY2025 level of $45.7 billion [F10]; a further decline would extend the downturn into a third year.
Watch the operating margin against the FY2024 level of 17.5% [F30] and the 12.1% window median [D1335], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch free cash flow against the FY2025 $6.1 billion [F100], with management forecasting lower equipment operating cash flow in 2026 [P6].
